case_studies.title: Fast Models, Slow Evidence: A Paired and Self-Audited Evaluation of System-1 Decision Models for LLM Agent Harnesses
case_studies.abstract: Agent harnesses make many small, typed decisions per task: which model to call, which tool to use, whether retrieved text is relevant, whether an input carries an injection. System-1 decision models answer such questions in a single forward pass with class probabilities, promising large cost and latency savings over LLM calls. We present a paired evaluation of an open-weight (Laya) and a hosted (Jev) System-1 model on 11 agent decision points built from 18 public sources: 7,283 base cases plus 6,640 robustness variants, with byte-identical inputs, paired tests, and cross-hardware and cross-day
case_studies.summary: The study evaluates quick, single-pass decision models (System‑1) that decide which LLM or tool to use in an agent harness, aiming to cut cost and latency. Researchers tested an open‑weight model and a hosted model on over 7,000 cases, showing how reliable decisions can replace slower, multi‑step checks. The results suggest significant efficiency gains for LLM‑driven workflows, but the work is mainly about model design rather than cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper introduces System-1 decision models that can rapidly make decisions about LLM calls and tool usage, which is directly relevant to engineers building LLM agent harnesses and could reduce cost and latency. The novelty comes from paired evaluation and self-auditing of open‑weight versus hosted models, offering surprising empirical insights that could prompt engineers to experiment with lightweight decision models in their pipelines. While the work is promising, the practical deployment steps and tool integrations are not fully detailed, limiting immediate actionability. The overall score is above 40, so the signal is not low.
